test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 21 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In a circle, chord AB subtends an angle of 75° at the circumference at point C. A tangent is drawn at point A. If the angle between this tangent and chord AC is 40°, what is the measure of the angle subtended by the minor arc AC at the center of the circle?
solution:
**Given:**

∠ACB = 75°

Angle between tangent at A and chord AC = 40°

**Formula Used:**

Angle between tangent and chord = Angle in opposite arc

Angle at center = 2 × Angle at circumference

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb8eba01452b6e012755ae4db36e1af8333056e0a22338295f47edf5dab07ee5.png] 

⇒ Angle between tangent and chord AC = Angle in opposite arc

⇒ ∠ABC = 40°

⇒ In △ABC:

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − (75° + 40°)

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 115°

⇒ ∠BAC = 65°

⇒ Minor arc AC subtends ∠ABC at circumference

⇒ ∠ABC = 40°

⇒ Angle at center = 2 × 40°

⇒ Angle at center = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**
